solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Skimpy bit of clothing — this part gets excited father turning round

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so the words this part gets are rearranged
turning round signals that the word for father is read backwards

parts.note: PA is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A fashion note: one daring part of a skimpy garment thrills Dad, who turns round in embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' looks like it describes father, but it is the anagram signal for the three words before it; 'turning round' applies only to father.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin shoulder strap on a dress or top, named after the pasta, is a skimpy piece of clothing.

clue.text: Hobbyist's prayer? Male pastor upset about that

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the rearranged letters go round the prayer
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a collect is a short prayer in Christian liturgy

explanation.surface: A hobbyist offers a prayer, and a male pastor is upset by it.
explanation.walkthrough: A collect is a short set prayer of the Anglican and Catholic liturgy. 'upset' jumbles the male letter with pastor, and 'about' wraps the result round the prayer; the 's after Hobbyist reads as 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A philatelist, who gathers postage stamps as a pastime, is a classic example of a hobbyist.

clue.text: When parking, come to a stop, doing for road surface

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
to halt is to come to a stop

explanation.surface: A driver's instruction: when parking, pull up, and that's what you do on the road surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmac-like bitumen material is laid as the surface of roads.

clue.text: Rash murmuring about a curious indication of injury

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the murmuring word goes round the rest

parts.note: a hum is a low murmuring sound
rum is an old-fashioned word for odd or curious
a scar is the mark an injury leaves

explanation.surface: Someone murmurs rashly about an odd mark that suggests an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like a skin complaint to go with injury, but it is the adjective reckless. 'about' has the murmur split round everything else; rum meaning strange is old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckless and impetuous behaviour is described by this rhyming idiom, a synonym for rash.

clue.text: Job security? Hurry up in support

indicators.note: in means placed inside the support word

parts.note: a tee is the small peg that supports a golf ball

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for hurry is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to run is to hurry

explanation.surface: A question about job security, then a call to hurry up and give support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the word for hurry, as this is a down clue, and 'in' sets it inside a golf tee, the support.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding a post permanently, especially in academia, gives a guaranteed job; the question mark marks the definition by description.

clue.text: Description of part of weather map is 'Nothing except a lot of ice'

definitions.text: Description of part of weather map

parts.note: taken as written
O, the zero figure, stands for nothing
bar means except, as in 'all bar one'

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the word ice loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster's caption: the chart shows nothing but heaps of ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims ICE to IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines joining points of equal pressure on a weather chart are called by this adjective, so it describes part of the map.

clue.text: Anything vulgar upset couple

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: owt is a Northern English dialect word for anything, so a colloquial or vulgar form

explanation.surface: Anything crude upsets the couple.
explanation.walkthrough: OWT is Northern English dialect for 'anything'; 'upset' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair or couple amounts to that number of things.

clue.text: A question, I fear, that excludes a water-source

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: that excludes means the word fear is written without the following letter

explanation.surface: A question that I fear rules out one water supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that excludes a' drops the A from FEAR, leaving FER.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground layer of rock holding water, tapped by wells and springs, is a source of water.

clue.text: Film punting excursion?

definitions.meaning: a 1937 Marx Brothers comedy has this title
punting is betting, so a trip to the horse racing for a flutter

explanation.surface: A film about a day out on a punt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punting' suggests boating on a river, but here it means betting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marx Brothers film title also literally describes a betting outing to watch horses run.

clue.text: Hoping for reduction in medicine

indicators.note: reduction means cutting short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to be aspiring to something is to be hoping for it

explanation.surface: Someone hoping for a cut in their medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduction' trims the final G from ASPIRING.
explanation.definitionFit: A common painkiller, acetylsalicylic acid, is a familiar medicine.

clue.text: Sonorous noise not initially containing nonsense

indicators.note: containing means the shortened word holds the nonsense inside it
not initially means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a sound is a noise
rot is nonsense

explanation.surface: A sonorous noise that, at first, does not hold any nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' beheads the word for noise, and 'containing' has it hold the nonsense word; rot for nonsense is British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A full, resonant, booming voice or style is called orotund, much like sonorous.

clue.text: Run out of fruit and veg

indicators.note: out of means taken away from the fruit word

parts.note: a pear is a fruit
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: The greengrocer has run out of fruit and vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes R from PEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A small green legume is a common vegetable, here shortened to veg.

clue.text: Fairy having month without part of body elf hexed

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the month goes around the other pieces

parts.note: May is a month
an organ is a part of the body

indicators.note: hexed means bewitched, so the letters of elf are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fairy, in her month, bewitches an elf's body part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense 'outside', so the month surrounds the rest; 'hexed' jumbles elf.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arthurian enchantress, half-sister of King Arthur, was known as a fairy queen.

clue.text: Pistol about to silence Jack, not Judge offering support for cases?

indicators.note: about means the pistol word goes around the silencing word

parts.note: a Luger is a German pistol
to gag is to silence

indicators.note: not means the following letter is dropped from Jack

explanation.surface: A pistol is used to silence Jack, though not the judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has the German pistol round the silencing word, and 'not' strikes the judge's letter from Jack. The question mark flags that these cases are suitcases.
explanation.definitionFit: An overhead shelf in a train holds suitcases, so it supports cases; the question mark flags the play on cases.

clue.text: African Christian is displacing introduction of creation science

indicators.note: displacing means pushing out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Coptic describes the Egyptian Christian church, and is gives 's, so Coptic's

indicators.note: introduction of means the first letter of the word creation

explanation.surface: An African Christian replaces the teaching of creation with science.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' gives S as in Coptic's; 'displacing' removes the first letter of 'creation', a C, from COPTICS.
explanation.definitionFit: The branch of physics concerned with light and vision is a science.

clue.text: Type of pyramid — woven Giza rug has back of it

indicators.note: woven means twisted together, so the letters are rearranged
back of means the last letter of the word it

explanation.surface: A woven rug from Giza with a pyramid pattern on the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' rearranges GIZA RUG; 'back of it' adds T.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepped temple tower of ancient Mesopotamia is a kind of pyramid.

clue.text: Source of Merlot (as clued in error)

definitions.text: Source of Merlot (as clued in error)

indicators.note: source of means the first letter of the word Merlot
in error means mistaken, so the letters of as clued are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wine buff's correction: the clue wrongly names Merlot as the source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' rearranges AS CLUED into USCADEL after the M. As a whole, the clue admits its grape is named wrongly: the real grape is this one, not Merlot.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscadel is a muscat grape and its sweet wine, the grape the clue should have named instead of Merlot.

clue.text: A sign of fire damage in chimney looks like plant

indicators.note: in means placed inside the chimney word

parts.note: lum is a Scottish word for chimney
a burn is a mark left by fire

explanation.surface: A sign of fire damage inside the chimney looks like a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Lum is Scots for chimney, a word British crosswords use often; 'in' puts A and the fire mark inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tree with hanging yellow flowers, often called golden chain, is a plant.

clue.text: Plates finally carried by servant, active fellow

indicators.note: carried by means held inside the servant word

parts.note: a butler is a household servant

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word Plates

explanation.surface: A busy servant finally brings in the plates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried by' puts S, the last letter of 'Plates', inside BUTLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who bustles about energetically is an active, busy person.

clue.text: What possibly inculcates jolly hospitable attitude?

indicators.note: inculcates means instils, so the jolly abbreviation is put inside
possibly means the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: Asks what might instil a jolly, welcoming attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective, but it is old naval slang for a Royal Marine. 'possibly' jumbles What, and 'inculcates' sets the marine inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendliness and cordiality towards guests is a kind of emotional heat, an apt sense here.

clue.text: Conflict restrained by bloke's computer programs

indicators.note: restrained by means held inside the word for bloke

parts.note: a bloke is a male; the 's is read as a link, is
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A conflict is held in check by some bloke's computer programs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restrained by' sets the conflict inside the bloke; the 's reads as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Malicious software such as viruses and spyware is a kind of computer program.

clue.text: One regulation I'd promoted for Indian festival

indicators.note: promoted means moved up, so in a down clue the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a law is a regulation
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone would promote one regulation for an Indian festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' turns ILAWID upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hindu festival of lights, held in autumn, is a major Indian festival.

clue.text: Device for shoppers remains cordoned off by working mechanic

indicators.note: cordoned off by means enclosed, so the remains word sits inside
working means being reworked, so the letters of mechanic are rearranged

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A shop device's remains are fenced off while a mechanic works on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' jumbles mechanic, and 'cordoned off by' encloses the remains in it, after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A street ATM dispenses banknotes, so it is a device shoppers use.

clue.text: Reduction in traditional knowledge leads to concerned exclamation

indicators.note: reduction in means the word is cut short at the end

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: Cutbacks in traditional learning provoke an anxious cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduction in' drops the final E of LORE. LOR is a colloquial British form of 'Lord!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial form of Lord, said in alarm or surprise, is a worried exclamation.

clue.text: Indebted former schoolfellow misled, getting grand invested

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: invested means placed inside, so the grand letter goes into the word

parts.note: lied means told falsehoods, so misled
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A former schoolmate in debt misled people, with a thousand put into the scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' puts G inside LIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling obliged to someone means owing them gratitude, so being indebted.

clue.text: Good type of radiation, mate

parts.note: UV is ultraviolet, a type of radiation

explanation.surface: A good kind of radiation, mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for governor, it is a matey British form of address, like mate.

clue.text: A male's account involving one historic speech

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep; the 's is a link

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the account letters go around one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man's account of a famous historic speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts I inside AC.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Semitic language thought to be spoken by Jesus is a historic tongue, speech meaning language.

clue.text: A stricken vessel at sea with no end of dire journey trouble

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged
with no means one letter is left out of the jumbled phrase
end of means the last letter of the word dire

explanation.surface: A stricken ship at sea, short of a dire ending, makes for a troubled voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges A STRICKEN VESSEL, and 'with no end of dire' removes one E from the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea brought on by motion in cars, ships or planes is a trouble of travelling.
